questions.stem: A body was recovered from an abandoned house with stiffening all joints. Which of the following statement is not true regarding the order of appearance of rigor mortis?

options.label: A
options.text: It appears first in involuntary muscles

options.label: B
options.text: It appears first in the myocardium

options.label: C
options.text: It appears in the lower limbs before the upper limbs

options.label: D
options.text: It disappears last from the small muscles of the fingers

questions.answerText: It appears in the lower limbs before the upper limbs
questions.solutionHtml:
It appears in the lower limbs before the upper limbs

Rigor mortis usually appears in the upper and lower limbs first.

  • Rigor mortis begins in the eyelids, neck and lower jaw and passes upwards to the muscles of the face, downwards to the muscles of the chest, upper limbs, abdomen and lower limbs and lastly, in the fingers and toes.
  • In individual limbs, it usually progresses from above downwards. Such a sequence is not constant, symmetrical or regular. In individual limbs, it disappears in the same order it has appeared. Rigor mortis always sets in, increases and decreases gradually.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 35th Edition, Page Number: 117, 118

questions.stem: Rigor mortis or cadaveric rigidity is because of the loss of ATP after death. It leads to sustained muscular contraction. False statement about cadaveric rigidity is:

options.label: C
options.text: It disappears in the sequence as it appears

questions.solutionHtml:
Seen immediately after death

Rigor mortis is not seen immediately after death. It starts one or two hours after death.

  • Rigor mortis (death stiffening; cadaveric rigidity) is a state of stiffening of muscles, sometimes with slight shortening of the fibres.
  • Individual cell death takes place in this stage.
  • All muscles of the body, both voluntary and involuntary, are affected.
  • It does not start in all muscles simultaneously (Nysten's rule).
  • It first appears _in involuntary muscles; the myocardium becomes rigid in an hour.
  • In India, it begins one to two hours after death and takes another two hours to develop.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 35th Edition, Page Number: 117, 118, 119

Myocardium
  1. Rigor mortis first appears in involuntary muscles; the myocardium becomes rigid in an hour.
  2. It begins in the eyelids, neck and lower jaw and passes upwards to the muscles of the face, downwards to the muscles of the chest, upper limbs, abdomen and lower limbs and lastly, in the fingers and toes.
  3. The lactic acid entered the bloodstream and reconverted to glycogen in the liver.
  4. In individual limbs, it usually progresses from above downwards. Such a sequence is not constant, symmetrical or regular.
  5. In individual limbs, it disappears in the same order it has appeared.
  6. Rigor mortis always sets in, increases and decreases gradually.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 35th Edition, Page Number: 117, 118, 119

options.label: C
options.text: Appears at the same time in the heart and eyelid

questions.solutionHtml:
Heart
  • The image demonstrates rigor mortis, appearing first in the heart.
  • The Order of Appearance of Rigor Mortis:-

  • It first appears in involuntary muscles; the myocardium becomes rigid in an hour.
  • It begins in the eyelids, neck and lower jaw and passes upwards to the muscles of the face, downwards to the muscles of the chest, upper limbs, abdomen and lower limbs and lastly, in the fingers and toes.
  • The lactic acid entered the bloodstream and reconverted to glycogen in the liver.
  • In individual limbs, it usually progresses from above downwards. Such a sequence is not constant, symmetrical or regular.
  • In individual limbs, it disappears in the same order in which it has appeared. Rigor mortis always sets in, increases and decreases gradually.

questions.stem: A forensic expert comes to the crime scene and assesses the rigor of the dead body. Which of the following is incorrect about the method of assessment of rigor?

options.label: D
options.text: He gently bends the knee joint

questions.solutionHtml:
He taps the glabella
  • Testing of Rigor mortis: - Rigor is tested by trying to lift the eyelids, depressing the jaw, and gently bending the neck and various joints of the body.
  • Note the degree (absent, minimal, moderate, advanced or complete) and distribution.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 35th Edition, Page Number: 117, 118, 119

questions.stem: A suicide person was found gripping the gun in his right hand. Which of the following statement about 'cadaveric spasm' is not true?

options.label: B
options.text: All muscles of the body are involved

options.label: C
options.text: Great force is required to overcome it

options.label: D
options.text: It indicates the manner of death

questions.answerText: All muscles of the body are involved
questions.solutionHtml:
All muscles of the body are involved

The phenomenon doesn't involve all the muscles of the body. It usually is limited to a small group of voluntary muscles.

  1. Cadaveric spasm (cataleptic rigidity) is a rare condition.
  2. (Option A) In this, the muscles contracted during life become stiff and rigid immediately after death without passing into the stage of primary relaxation.
  3. As such, the change preserves the exact attitude of the person at the time of death for several hours afterwards. The spasm is primarily a vital phenomenon that originates from normal nervous stimulation of the muscles.
  4. (Option B and D) This is usually limited to a single group of voluntary muscles and frequently involves the hands. Occasionally, the whole body is affected, as seen in soldiers shot in battle, when the body may retain the posture that it assumed at the moment of death.
  5. It is not easy to simulate this condition because of the muscles' powerful contraction, which is impossible to recreate artificially.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 35th Edition, Page Number: 119
